es onward like stream to eternity

branches. But chill November comes,
bringing bowling winds and 'melan-
cholly days the saddest of the
year" The year is now far advanced.
Only one more month remains and that
soon passes and the Old Year dies and
another New Year takes its place and
the old is soon forgotten.


Thus is life. Old friends are forgot
ten and laid aside to give place to new
ones. Our highest hopes and ambitions
Of one year are changed the next and
even il we reach the goal our greatest
glory and ambition fade before grim
Death and sink into nothingness. And
so is our life. We are born so die
Life is short, but oh, what changes it
has Joy and sorrow are commingled
and our tears and smiles are blending
together, till at last comes the end,
when our dead hopes are buried with
us, and We await the great resurrection,
which will bring new hopes and aSpira-
tions, when time shall be no more.

The campaign in Tunisia has not been
holiday parade as the French staff fancied it
would b.. The invading columns were in mo-
ton on April 26, and within twelve days
battery was displayed at the gates of the Bey's
palace The principally had been overrun
under a hollow pretext for the Kroumirs had
not menaced the security of Eastern Algeria,
hut had laid down their arms at the request of
the Bey before marching orders were given to
the French troops. The capital had been ap-
preached, the treaty of peace dictated, and
the country virtually annexed under false
pretences, for these unjustifable measures were
in violation of positive pledges to the Bey and
to the European Powers. There had been no
fighting, for there were no KrOumirs in the
field. There had been q fortnight Of easy
marching, and the mobility of the new military
system had been demonstrated. A bold stroke
had been planned and executed at small ex-
pense. Military prestige had been gained, and
nothing had been sacrificed except good faith
and diplomatic honesty. The helpless Bey had
been bullied and the British and Italian
courts duped; the Nation had suddenly emerged
from retirement and done something that
was bold, aggressive and dashing, albeit
somewhat immoral, and the troops were ready
to reembark for Marseilles after an ENJOYABLE
excursion in the principally.


The illusion was soon dispelled. The French
lad not lighted a torch that would illumne
that benighted region with the blessings Of
commerce and civilization. They had kindled
a fanaticism that would spread from tribe to
tribe throughout Northern Africa. First came
a revolt in Constantine next an instruction
in Oran then fire and slaughter in the Span
ish settlements, when Bou Amena appeared
from his hiding-place in the desert and
finally the tribes of Southern Tunisia banded
together against the Bey and his new ally.
Now the fighting was to begin in earnest, for
when Sfax was battered down by the fleet its
six hundred defenders remained in the ruins,
firing slowly but steadily until they were over
powered by superior numbers. One tribe after
another renowned allegiance to sovereign
who was charged with bctraying the Calph
and leaving the holy places to their fate.

corded. Reduced to its simple

ing Rosina Knight, his first wife,

riage with Caroline Drake was

ingly ordered George Merrifisld
